statement: The quasi-quadratic involution and polarization manipulations used on108–110 are identities of quadratic laws under the stated axioms, not merely functions on a finite set of base-ring points.
computation: Forx, n(σx)=n(x) as in CL-SA02-013. Forx,y,φ(x,y)=t(x)t(y)−t(xy) follows by expandingt(xσy); polarization of CH then gives the multiplication formula. These are universal quadratic identities, so arbitrary base change is handled by Roby PropII.1 rather than point sampling.
fate: The computational identities are valid with the stated scalar polarization axiom. The finite Z/4 check is supplemented by an explicit universal law and does not substitute for it. Search audit: Q02.

statement: Refined statement of CL-SA02-028: a Γ-stable closed subscheme of a finite transitive constant Γ-scheme overR is the whole scheme ifR injects into its own global functions, not merely those of the ambient scheme.

fate: This is the corrected elementary lemma used in CL-SA02-027. It refines the false literal target and adds the closedness actually required by the ideal proof. The manuscript transcription itself is unchanged. Search audit: Q03.
